catalog_quote: <초분절요소> 어휘의 채록 과정에서 일부 단어에서 고성조를 가진 모음이 약간 길게 발음되는 경우가 있었지만 이러한 장모음이 변별적 기능을 갖는 경우는 발견할 수 없었다. 강세 현상도 일부 형태-통사적 환경(예: 복수 접미사 {-́xà})에서 나타나기는 하지만 전반적으로 흔하지는 않다. 이와 같은 현상들은 세 언어 모두 공통적이라고 할 수 있다. 어휘 목록에서 보다시피 모든 단어에 대해 성조가 표시되어 있는데 이는 단순히 본 연구자가 직접 청취한대로 전사한 결과로서 아직 성조의 기능적 실체를 정확히 밝혀내지는 못했다. 그 이유는 청각적으로 고성조와 저성조 간의 높낮이가 하우사어나 요루바어와 같은 다른 전형적인 성조어들처럼 그다지 뚜렷하지 않은데다가 또한 채록된 언어자료에서 성조가 변별적 기능을 하는 환경들을 아직 발견하지 못했기 때문이다. 그러나 현재까지의 분석 결과를 놓고 볼 때 이 세 언어 모두에서 성조의 기능적 부담(functional load)은 그리 크지 않은 것으로 보인다.

new_statements.translation: <Suprasegmentals> During elicitation of the vocabulary, in some words a vowel bearing high tone was pronounced somewhat long, but no case could be found in which such long vowels have a distinctive function. Stress phenomena, too, appear in some morpho-syntactic environments (e.g. the plural suffix {-́xà}), but on the whole they are not common. These phenomena can be said to be common to all three languages [Cinene, Glavda, Guduf]. As can be seen in the word list, tone is marked on every word, but this is simply the result of transcribing exactly as the researcher heard it; the functional substance of tone has not yet been precisely established. The reason is that auditorily the pitch difference between high and low tone is not as clear as in other typical tone languages such as Hausa or Yoruba, and moreover no environments in which tone functions distinctively have yet been found in the recorded data. Judging from the analysis so far, however, the functional load of tone in all three languages appears not to be great. [2009 report version adds: 'This holds not only for Cinene and Glavda but equally for Guduf, which has been comparatively well studied as the subject of my doctoral thesis', with fn. 5: 'Guduf has a high tone and a low tone, but as far as established so far their lexical or grammatical distinctive function has proved extremely limited.' Kim 2006 p. 39 on Guduf: 'Two tones are distinguished (H á, L à) but their functional load is relatively weak; therefore not marked in the orthography. No vowel-length contrast.']

new_statements.rule_in_words: No positional word-stress rule is described. The only first-hand description (Kim, own fieldwork 1999/2001) treats Guduf (with Cinene and Glavda) as having two register tones (H, L) of low functional load and weak phonetic salience, no contrastive vowel length, and 'stress phenomena' only as marginal, morphosyntactically conditioned prominence (e.g. associated with the plural suffix -́xà, which carries/induces a high pitch), 'on the whole not common'. I.e. stress is not presented as a regular word-level property and no default stress position (initial/penult/final) is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: Stress-like prominence noted only in certain morpho-syntactic environments, exemplified by the plural suffix {-́xà} (waɣà 'goat' > waɣa-xà); occasional non-contrastive lengthening of high-toned vowels.
new_statements.domain_note: Based on elicited lexical items (c. 650-word list) and questionnaire sentences from the author's 1999 and 2001 fieldwork in the Gwoza area; statement is impressionistic (author explicitly says the tonal system is not yet worked out) and is made jointly for Cinene, Glavda and Guduf; citation-form words are transcribed with H/L tone, not stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted passage comes from Kim's description of Cinene [cie; Glottolog cine1238, which Kim regards as an offshoot of the Cikide dialect of Guduf], but the suprasegmental findings are explicitly asserted to be 'common to all three languages' compared, i.e. Cinene, Glavda [glav1244] and Guduf [gudu1252]; the 2009 report version adds that this holds equally for Guduf, the object of Kim's (unfinished) Leipzig dissertation, and Kim 2006 p. 39 gives the Guduf-specific tone/length statement. Kim's Guduf data are his own 1999/2001 fieldwork in the Gwoza Hills (Borno State, Nigeria); his comparative wordlists are labelled 'Guduf-Cikide' and he distinguishes the dialects Gava (Yaghwatadaxa), Bubayagwa and Cikide. The older German sources (Büchner 1964, Scheytt 1966/67, Rapp 1966/1968) describe the Gava dialect (Yaghwatadaxa, Glottolog gava1240) from the Basel Mission station at Gava.

sources.note: §3.1 (pp. 139-141) gives consonant/vowel charts and a <suprasegmentals> paragraph explicitly stated to hold for all three languages compared (Cinene, Glavda, Guduf; author's own 1999/2001 fieldwork): occasional non-distinctive lengthening of high-toned vowels; 'stress phenomena also appear in some morpho-syntactic environments (e.g. the plural suffix {-́xà}) but are on the whole not common'; H/L tone transcribed but pitch difference not salient and no distinctive tonal environments found; functional load of tone low in all three. No default word-stress position is given.

sources.citation: Kim, Hak-Soo. 2009. 치네네어(Cinene, 북동나이지리아)의 언어적 특징과 계통적 지위에 관한 고찰 - 결과보고서 [NRF/KRF final research report, project KRF-2007-551-A00089]. 33 pp. KRM metaDataId 4b76f6dc2c90a691012c9b9b9bd92e8a. In Korean.

sources.citation: Kim, Hak-Soo. 2006. 아프리카언어들의 표기에 관한 연구: 나이지리아의 구두프(Guduf)어와 치네네(Cinene)어의 표기를 중심으로 - 결과보고서 [A study on writing African languages, focused on an orthography for Guduf and Cinene (Nigeria); NRF final report, 2004 programme]. 48 pp. KRM metaDataId 4b6f22e31b4e911b011b4f8b22a32970. In Korean.
sources.note: Topic C (pp. 35-41) is Guduf-specific: consonant and vowel phoneme charts, positional vowel system, and p. 39 '(3) 성조/장단: 두 개의 성조가 구분되지만(고성조 á, 저성조 à), 그 기능 부담성은 상대적으로 약함. 따라서 표기법에서는 표시하지 않음. 모음의 장단 구분 없음.' (Tone/length: two tones are distinguished, H á and L à, but their functional load is relatively weak, so they are not. no vowel-length contrast). Glossed Guduf text with tone marks follows. Nothing on stress.
